drivers.name: Recent trend
drivers.why: Over the last 30 days the price fell 13.4% once the usual seasonal effect is taken out. The forecast carries that direction forward but lets it fade each day, so about 65% of it is kept over the next 30 days.

drivers.name: Season
drivers.why: In the seasonal pattern (from 9 years of prices) the price is usually 0.5% lower in 30 days' time (Nov) than now (Oct).

drivers.name: Last few days' average
drivers.why: Today's price is below the last 5 days' average, and the forecast counts a one-day dip only half, so it starts 0.8% higher than today.

forecast_reason.range: 80% of past misses fell inside -23.1% to +8.7% at 30 days, so that is the likely range.
forecast_reason.trust: Tested on 244 past dates: off by 11.1% on average at 30 days, vs 9.6% for "price stays the same" - it is NOT better than no-change here, so read it as a range, not a number. Direction right 54% of the time.
forecast_reason.blind: It reads only the price's own trend and season. It can't see US interest-rate moves, war or crisis news, central-bank buying, or an import-duty change in the Budget - news like that can move the price outside the range.
